findings.title: task add-pdp-cedar-fix-2/1.1: the M8 entry of malformed.test.ts still uses the wrong text
findings.detail: The fix finding asked for the M8 text in the malformed-policy test to be replaced with design.md's `permit (principal, action == Action::"reed", resource);`. In src/pdp/malformed.test.ts the M8 entry still reads `@id("bad") permit (principal, action == Action::"read", resource == Action::"reed");`. The implementer's note says this line was replaced; the diff shows it was not. The design case is now tested only in the new src/pdp/malformed.m8.test.ts, so the test named 'M8 malformed policy is refused' still checks a different fault.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the M8 text in src/pdp/malformed.test.ts with design.md's M8 text, or drop that entry in favour of malformed.m8.test.ts.

findings.title: An egress of null denies instead of counting as absent
findings.detail: guards.ts sets `hasEgress: egress !== undefined`, so `egress: null` goes to validateEgress, fails, and the request is denied. An implementation that treats null as 'no egress' would allow it with no permit instead. No scenario pins this case.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an otherwise allowed request carries `egress: null` THEN check returns `deny` with errors ["PDP_REQUEST_INVALID"] and no permit.

findings.title: A non-plain object nested in attrs or context makes the request invalid
findings.detail: snapshotValue throws for any nested object whose prototype is neither Object.prototype nor null (for example a Date or a class instance), so check denies with PDP_REQUEST_INVALID. Another implementation could pass such a value through JSON to Cedar instead. The spec only pins that `context` itself must be a plain object.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an entity attribute or a context value holds a non-plain object such as a Date THEN check returns `deny` with errors ["PDP_REQUEST_INVALID"] and reasons [].

findings.title: toDecimal accepts values Cedar decimal cannot hold
findings.detail: toDecimal only checks that Number(n.toFixed(4)) === n. For |n| >= 1e21, toFixed returns exponential notation, so toDecimal(1e21) returns arg "1e+21". Values above Cedar's decimal range (about 9.22e14) also pass, for example 1e15 → "1000000000000000.0000". Cedar would reject either one later, as PDP_REQUEST_INVALID at check.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN toDecimal runs on 1e21 THEN it returns {__extn:{fn:"decimal",arg:"1e+21"}} without throwing.

findings.title: An egress of null denies instead of counting as absent
findings.detail: guards.ts sets `hasEgress: egress !== undefined`, so `egress: null` goes to validateEgress, fails, and the request is denied. An implementation that treats null as 'no egress' would allow it with no permit instead. No scenario pins this case.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an otherwise allowed request carries `egress: null` THEN check returns `deny` with errors ["PDP_REQUEST_INVALID"] and no permit.

findings.title: A non-plain object nested in attrs or context makes the request invalid
findings.detail: snapshotValue throws for any nested object whose prototype is neither Object.prototype nor null (for example a Date or a class instance), so check denies with PDP_REQUEST_INVALID. Another implementation could pass such a value through JSON to Cedar instead. The spec only pins that `context` itself must be a plain object.

      throw new TypeError("request value is not a plain object");
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN an entity attribute or a context value holds a non-plain object such as a Date THEN check returns `deny` with errors ["PDP_REQUEST_INVALID"] and reasons [].

findings.title: toDecimal accepts values Cedar decimal cannot hold
findings.detail: toDecimal only checks that Number(n.toFixed(4)) === n. For |n| >= 1e21, toFixed returns exponential notation, so toDecimal(1e21) returns arg "1e+21". Values above Cedar's decimal range (about 9.22e14) also pass, for example 1e15 → "1000000000000000.0000". Cedar would reject either one later, as PDP_REQUEST_INVALID at check.
